use normalization_adapter::Normalizer;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

#[test]
fn lexical_corpus() {
    let normalizer = Normalizer::new().unwrap();
    let cases: Vec<Value> = serde_json::from_str(include_str!("cases.json")).unwrap();
    for (index, case) in cases.iter().enumerate() {
        let branch = case["branch"].as_str().unwrap();
        let input = case["input"].as_str().unwrap();
        let result = match case["mode"].as_str() {
            Some("base64") => normalizer.normalize_base64_json(branch, input),
            Some("value") => normalizer.normalize_value(branch, &serde_json::from_str(input).unwrap()),
            _ => normalizer.normalize(branch, input),
        };
        match result {
            Ok(value) => assert_eq!(Some(&value), case.get("value"), "case {index}"),
            Err(error) => assert_eq!(Some(json!(error.0)), case.get("errors").cloned(), "case {index}"),
        }
    }
    // The retained enclosing document is explicitly decoded before nested capture.
    let outer = normalizer.normalize("root", r#"{"payload": {"n":1e999,"n":2}}"#).unwrap();
    let inner = normalizer.normalize_base64_json("record", outer.as_str().unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(inner, json!({"payload":"eyJuIjoxZTk5OSwibiI6Mn0="}));
}
